name: gi bleeding overview
title: GI bleeding decision chart: resuscitate and correct coagulopathy first, then sort by the ligament of Treitz; an upper bleed is non-variceal (IV pantoprazole and endoscopic therapy) or variceal (pantoprazole, octreotide, antibiotics, banding), a lower bleed goes to colonoscopy if stable or to upper endoscopy, angiography and surgery if unstable

root.title: GI bleed: RESUSCITATE first, then UPPER or LOWER (the ligament of Treitz)?
lines: airway (intubate if needed) · 2 large-bore IVs · fluids · transfuse
correct coagulopathy: fresh frozen plasma, platelets, vitamin K, Octaplex · STOP anticoagulants and antiplatelets
NO visible blood (OCCULT: positive fecal occult blood or iron deficiency anemia) → rule out colorectal and other cancers

groups.title: UPPER: HEMATEMESIS or MELENA
lines: • ↑ urea : creatinine, or fresh blood up a nasogastric tube
• HIGHER MORTALITY: age > 60, shock, heart disease or cirrhosis, fresh red blood, bleeding that persists or starts in hospital
• urgent esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) AFTER resuscitation: finds AND treats

groups.title: LOWER: HEMATOCHEZIA · is the patient STABLE?
lines: • inflammatory bowel disease, cancer, ischemic or infectious colitis, radiation, post-polypectomy
